findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in the physical facility in need of repair.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: All temperature control for food safety (TCS) food items were observed to be out of temperature in the facility’s prep cooler. Items include, but are not limited to: ham (64F), ham salad (69F), chicken breasts (70F), roast beef (65F), and ham salad (64F). CORRECTED- items that had been in the unit for over 4 hours were voluntarily discarded. Items that had been in the unit for less than 2 hours were either moved to time as control or moved to the working standing cooler. TCS foods must be used or discarded within 4 hours after being removed from temperature control (41F and under for cold holding).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The prep cooler was observed to have an ambient temperature of 60F, and is failing to hold TCS foods at temperature- see violation #22. The PIC stated the AC in the building is scheduled to be fixed the following morning, and that will hopefully prevent the unit from over working. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 6/15/26 to verify that the prep cooler is holding TCS foods at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Lettuce in the top right holding compartment of the sandwich prep cooler was observed with an internal temperature of 50F. Manager confirmed temperature with the facility’s calibrated stem thermometer. Lettuce was washed and cut around 10am and stacked with other containers in the 2 door cooler prior to storage in the prep cooler for service within the hour prior to inspector’s arrival. All coolers were observed holding below 40F, and other foods in coolers were at proper temperature. Lettuce was in a plastic container and wrapped tightly, so that storage in combination with being stacked may not have allowed for chilling after prep. Lettuce will be served or discarded by 7:30pm.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.citation_text:

However, that employee was not the PIC, and their shift concluded before 5pm. Designated PIC at time of inspection plans to complete an online course in the upcoming week and take certification exam at the end of the month.  
 Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-403.12 Issue with ponding condensation was improved since the previous inspection but not resolved. PIC noted the owners came in to adjust the cooler, which resulted in condensation accumulating at a slower rate. However, ponding condensation is still an issue in the bottom of the cooler. Upon further investigation it would appear the condensing unit has ponding water that may be seeping from the back ledge to the bottom inside the cooler. Moisture was visible along the edge of the shelving on the back ledge, and accumulation of condensation was observed in the cooler on the bottom left side. Owners need to have the prep cooler serviced by a licensed refrigeration technician. **See general comments for additional information**
Condensate drainage and other non-sewage liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to law.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Store manager has a food handler certification but has not yet completed a course to obtain his food manager certification. Information was provided for locations to attend a food manager course. 

Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was observed working the cash register and answering the phone prior to putting on gloves to prepare food without first washing his hands. Handwashing between tasks and proper technique were discussed. 
Employee washed his hands prior to continuing with his next task and several times between tasks before the end of his shift. Educational handouts on when to wash hands and glove use were provided.

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Soups in the back warmer were nowhere near proper temperature. Two soups (one reheat and one a first time heat as of today) had surface and internal temperatures 106°F-117°F. Products in question were in the warmer since the start of business and were discarded. Another soup that was just opened and placed in the warmer around 130p had an internal temperature of ~100°F. Warmer was turned up to rapidly heat the soup prior to proper hot holding at 135°F. 
NOTE: The water in the bottom of the warmer was only 121°F prior to the dial being adjusted to a higher setting for heating purposes. Make sure warmers are set at proper temperature as needed to allow for proper heating and hot holding. Consider placing metal pans through the oven prior to hot holding and/or rotating products between the warmers for heating and hot holding stages.
 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 A generic chemical spray bottle hanging in the back storage area had multiple options to mark for labeling as to the contents. The bottle was not labeled. Manager thought it was likely degreaser. The chemical was discarded during the inspection.
Another bottle that said "table top cleaner" along the top and had a quat sanitizer label contained a very strong chlorine based solution. Inspector's test strip was almost bleached out by the solution. The solution in question was discarded during the inspection. 
Proper labeling of chemical spray bottles was discussed. 

Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site (bleach solution) shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Metal stem thermometer had not been calibrated in a few months based on information provided. When thermometer was checked in ice water solution it was observed around 40°F. Food thermometer was properly calibrated during inspection to 32°F in the ice water solution. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.

Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use. Calibrate food thermometers frequently to ensure accuracy when monitoring food temperatures.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA 100-0367, Section 3.07  Manager stated a night manager and the night driver each have a food manager certification; however, proof of certifications were not available. Proof of food allergen awareness certifications were also not present. All certified food managers need to complete the online food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection. Requirements for allergen training were discussed, and information was provided for management to find an online course.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
(R) 750.120 - Slimy mold accumulation was again observed in the ice machine around the opening in the ceiling where ice comes out. Condensation droplets were gathered on the mold but not dripping onto the ice. A barrier of sandwich paper was placed on the ice, and the store manager wiped the area in question with a bleach solution during the inspection. Layer of ice was removed once the process was completed. Manager was advised on cleaning and sanitizing (quarterly maintenance provided by outside company). 

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine as needed to eliminate buildup of mold.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.510 & 512 - Paper towel dispenser at kitchen handsink was empty. Employee doing dishes stated the store didn't have paper towels. Upon furhter questioning, manager stated paper towels ran out the evening prior at the kitchen handsink; paper towels were available in both restrooms. Hands were being washed in the restroom now and then. Without the presence of paper towels or even napkins at the kitchen handsink, proper handwashing was not happening between glove changes and after handling money since the dispenser ran out the evening prior. Manager sent employee to get paper towels; three rolls of paper towels were obtained from another location for use until the next delivery is received. 

Employee returned from getting paper towels and then began looking at his cell phone while changing out dish water at the 3 part sink. Employee then removed previously soaking dishes from the sanitizer solution without first washing hands. Employee was advised on handwashing and then washed his hands without proper technique. The process took less than 10 seconds, he didn't lather hands, didn't properly dry hands or use paper towels as a barrier to shut off the manual faucet. Employee was advised to use the proper handwashing technique poster above the handsink for guidance; it has the proper process listed step by step. 
Handwashing was discussed at length with the store manager and maintaining supplies for proper handwashing was stressed.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, upon returning to the facility/before doing anything, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. 
Have paper towels dispensed and ready to dry hands prior to beginning handwashing process. Use paper towels to dry hands and then use paper towels as a barrier to shut off the faucet as the final step of handwashing process.
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - An employee was also observed eating a sucker in the kitchen prep/dish area. The employee then proceeded to clean the floor in the dining area and was eating the sucker as he re-entered the kitchen and was standing at the 3 part sink preparing to do dishes. Employee was told he should not be eating candy while working, and the sucker stick was discarded.

Employees shall consume food, including candy, gum, mints, etc., only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection. **Do not eat in the food prep and service areas**

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
760.1060 - Urinal in men's room was out of order. Get the urinal repaired.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Paper towels were not available at the kitchen handsink upon arrival of inspector (see #12a).
Paper towels were provided.
Maintain a supply of soap and paper towels at all handsink to allow for proper handwashing. 

Men's room toilet was soiled inside and on the back behind the seat. Clean the men's room toilet.
All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Pastrami in 2 door cooler was dated with a prep date of  6/19 and use by date of 6/25. Pastrami was past the 7 day time frame for use. Product was discarded during the inspection.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food must be properly dated and used or discarded within 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Upon arrival employee was observed handling cell phone prior to approaching the front counter and retrieving gloves. Employee was later observed turning off the faucet without a barrier during handwashing.  Proper handwashing and when to wash hands were discussed.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves, and prior to working with food, clean equipment and unwrapped single service articles.
Educational handouts on handwashing and glove use provided.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Spray bottle of quat sanitizer was available for wiping down tables. Manager on duty stated the bottle was brought to their store by another manager that told them to use it for wiping down tables. Quat test strips are needed to check the concentration of the sanitizer provided in the spray bottle.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text:
750.1160 - Fruit flies were observed in the back of the facility, with the majority of flies, a dozen plus, noted under the 3 part sink on the wall, plumbing and around the floor drain. Another half dozen flies were observed between the wall by soda storage next to the 2 door cooler, by the computer in back, and around the mopsink. Manager on duty was advised on general cleaning and maintenance to help minimize the presence of flies. If cleaning and maintenance alone do not alleviate the issue, then contact pest control operator for service.
NOTE: Fly strips may be utilized under the 3 part sink and in other places that do not pose a potential risk of cross contamination to food, equipment, and single service articles.

Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750.1220 - Floor drain under the 3 part sink had accumulation of mold down inside. Clean down inside the floor drain. Buildup of mold may be serving as a potential food source for flies.

Floors, including drains, must be in good repair and maintained clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 - Plastic baseboard was observed to be loose along the floor juncture in a few spots under the 3 part sink. Re-seal along seams that are loose and may allow for an accumulation of debris/moisture, which can then contribute as a food and water source for flies and other pests.

Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
(R) 750.1210 & 1220 - DISH WASHING AREA
1. Caulk along the drain board and wall juncture on the right side of the 3 part sink was observed to be cracked and moldy. Remove moldy, cracked caulk and reseal the juncture.
2. Paint was peeling and mold accumulation was noted under the juncture where caulk has molded and cracked at the drain board and wall juncture. Clean and repaint the wall in this area.
3. Paint was bubbled, cracked, and missing at the corner under the 3 part sink. Repair and repaint the at the corner under the 3 part sink.
4. A piece of loose drywall was observed under the wash basin of the 3 part sink. It appeared to be a removable access panel. . The drywall was crumbling in a few spots, paint was peeling off of it, gaps were present, and transparent tape was observed to be used as a repair material to hold part of it in place. Make proper repairs to the wall access panel under the 3 part sink.
NOTE: Areas with mold and disrepair may contribute to the presence of fruit flies by providing a potential food source and locations for harborage. 

Walls and attached fixtures must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 REPEAT x 2: The following walls continue to be observed in disrepair: 1) the wall behind the steam table has chipped paint; 2) the short and narrow supports of the wall behind the soda station have been spackled and now need to be sanded and sealed; 3) the mop sink is observed with cracked and peeled caulking (recaulk the sink to the wall); asnd NEW 4) the caulking of the three compartment sink is observed molded and pulling from the wall on the backside and on the right side. Remove existing caulking and recaulk so the 3-part sink is properly sealed to the wall. All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510d Observed an employee place gloves on unwashed hands and begin handling washed lettuce. Discussed handwashing prior to glove use. Employee then improperly washed hands - acquiring papertowel after turning off water. Use a barrier to protect clean hands from contaminated faucets and towel dispensers. Extend papertowel before starting to wash hands. Use towel to turn off water. To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door. 750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to using gloves, handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed an employee beverage on top of the Ben and Jerry's Reach-In Freezer. Removed from top of freezer during the inspection. Store drinks away and beneath of any food storage and preparation areas. Treat drink as if it were to spill it would not cross-contaminate anything. Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-650a Cutting board being used to chop lettuce is constructed of plastic that has become so deeply cut that grooves cannot be adequately cleaned. Frequently used portions of the board are black with food and soil debris unable to be properly cleaned. Cease use of this cutting board. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Sani-bucket in the backroom has not been changed after lunch. Zero bleach was present within the solution. Change buckets frequently enough to maintain 100ppm Cl within the buckets. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 Single-service fork container on the frontline is observed soiled with paper garbage and crumb debris. Also, same container is holding forks handle to face and vice versa. Store forks in clean container with handle extending out of container - intent is to allow employee to grab handle and no the portion to be brought to customer's mouth. Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment: 750-1130(e) Mop water from cleaning activities is observed still in the bucket adjacent to the mop sink. Empty waste water immediately after use. Also, there is a leak at the wash sink of the 3-part sink. There appears to be a broken gasket and a seal that allows for waste water from washing activities. The waste water is being caught within an old food jar. Waste water has accumulated and become frothy. Make sure drain water is emptied daily and catch basin is cleaned daily. Repair the leak to keep floors free from liquid waste and prevent availability of water source for pests. Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 750-1170 Upon entering the facility, the backdoor was observed to be not tightly closed. During the inspection, door was shut tightly. Make sure door is allowed to properly swing shut and close tightly. Repair self-closer if necessary to insure door always closes tightly. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1200 REPEAT x 1: The coving along the wall from the right of the rolling bread cart to the left of the make table is either pulled or peeling away from the wall. Seal the coving to the wall to eliminate coving gaps for food the accumulate - especially around the make table. A picture of this was taken during the inspection. There is a good fist-full of dried prep table foods stuck within this gap. NEW: The coving directly beneath the soda machine (backline) is pulling from the wall, also, portion of coving to the right of the three part sink has pulled too.  The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch. 750-1220 REPEAT x 1:Floor drain beneath the 3-part sink is observed moldy. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 REPEAT x 1:The following wall & ceiling areas need repair attention: 1) section of wall is missing & soiled behind the water heater - provide slotted grate to allow for access to water valve; 2) chipped paint on wall directly behind steam table; 3) short & narrow support is damaged to right of cubby/CO2 tank storage; and 4) about 4 ceiling tiles above the breaker box  & above the water heater are observed water damaged. Repair or replace wall & ceilings as needed to maintain surfaces smooth, easily cleanable, in good repair. NEW: The mop sink is not properly caulked to the wall. AND the wall to the right of the backdoor is damaged. FINALLY, the plumbing beneath the 3-part sink is soiled. All walls & ceilings must be in good repair & constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination & infestation by insects & rodents.  Provide properly constructed walls & ceilings.

findings.title: Clean and soiled linen segregated and properly stored.
findings.comment: 750-1380a Linens are observed stored on the floor and draped over the mop sink. Properly stored clean linens in a clean, dry location. Soiled linens should be separated and ready for laundering. Clean clothes and linens shall be stored in a clean place and protected from contamination until used.  Properly store all linens.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750-540 There is currently no certified food handler present. All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.
